<description>
**Summary**. Refactor validation result to be a return value instead of an output parameter in several `validation.cpp` methods.

**Motivation**. The benefits of the change are:
- Exclude the potentially inconsistent case when the bool return value and the returned `state` are inconsistent
- Exclude the ambiguity whether the passed in value of state is used or not (not obvious in chained calls)
- Remove the possibility of unintuitive interaction between subsequent calls with the same state. In case of a validation error, a failure reason is set if the state was valid, but not if it was already invalid.
- Slightly simpler: It's more evident which is the result; one less parameters.

This has grown out from #33856, mentioned in [comment here](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/33856#pullrequestreview-4276791829) and [here](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/33856#issuecomment-4477751949).

**Details**. Many methods follow the scheme where the validation state is returned in an output parameter (`BlockValidationState& state`), and and additional `bool` return value indicating success. In success case the convention is that `state.IsValid()` and the return value are both true. After the change there is only a `BlockValidationState` return value, which is either success (`state.IsValid() == true`), or an invalid/error case.

This change is a highly localized refactor, but touching a sensitive file.

Relevant methods called by `ProcessNewBlockHeaders` and `AcceptBlock` (directly and indirectly) are touched.

Changes are separated into commits by touched methods, ordered by bottom-to-top in the call hierarchy.
</description>

Indeed there was a silent merge conflict, thanks for the heads-up @arejula27!
Rebase to current master is without conflict, but it results in code with compile error. #35714 added a `state.Error` line in `FlushStateToDisk`, and also some new calls in `src/test/chainstate_write_tests.cpp`. These have to be updated.

[2026-11-05] rc:4478285575 inline on src/validation.cpp by optout21 (member):
Indeed, good catch!
The old code did overwrite the state, but only partly. It 'upgraded' the error from Invalid to Error, but when doing so, the reject reason was kept. Now a new state is created, that will have the supplied new reason.

This is a slight behavior change (albeit small), I'm still mulling on how to deal with it:

- Workaround, add another logging (or just switch the order), so both reject reasons are logged. Keep the overwrite.
- Overwrite the Invalid state with a new Error one, but include the previous state (as string) in the new reject reason (and log).
- Change the behavior in a separate commit, so it's explicit. The reason is logged and overwritten.
- Mimic the old behavior, by always supplying `FatalError` with a previous state, and potentially preserving the reason string from there.
- Sort out the issue in a separate PR (for better visibility)

I was looking also for similar cases (`state = ...`, `MakeError`, `FatalError`). There are a handful of places to check (in `ConnectTip`, `ActivateBestChainStep`, `VerifyDB`).

Analyzing the old code, the `"Corrupt block..."` message was never stored in the state!

Details:

- `BLOCK_MUTATED` is always used with Invalid state, and one of the following reject reasons: `"bad-txnmrklroot"`, `"bad-txns-duplicate"`, `"bad-witness-nonce-size"`, `"bad-witness-merkle-match"`, `"unexpected-witness"`.
- when execution gets into the if branch, `state.m_mode` is `M_INVALID`
- `notifications.fatalError` is invoked with `"Corrupt block..."`
- `state.Error` is called
- mode is set to Error, but reject reason is not Changed
- Later logging uses the original reject reason

```C++
if (state.GetResult() == BlockValidationResult::BLOCK_MUTATED) {
    // We don't write down blocks to disk if they may have been
    // corrupted, so this should be impossible unless we're having hardware
    // problems.
    return FatalError(m_chainman.GetNotifications(), state, _("Corrupt block found indicating potential hardware failure."));
}
LogError("%s: Consensus::CheckBlock: %s\n", __func__, state.ToString());
```

```C++
bool FatalError(Notifications& notifications, BlockValidationState& state, const bilingual_str& message)
{
    notifications.fatalError(message);
    return state.Error(message.original);
}
```

```C++
bool Error(const std::string& reject_reason)
{
    if (m_mode == ModeState::M_VALID)
        m_reject_reason = reject_reason;
    m_mode = ModeState::M_ERROR;
    return false;
}
```
[2026-11-05] rc:4479200454 inline on src/validation.cpp by optout21 (member) (edited 2026-11-05):
I concluded that overwriting the rejection reason here is the right way to go, as a new, higher level error is created from the previous invalid result. Also, it's not recommended to mix Error status with Invalid-style reject reasons.
My fix is adding a specific log and comment about the upgrading of the error.

I've also checked for other potential places where an Invalid state can be upgraded to Error, but found none (checked changed in `validation.cpp`, especially around the patterns `state = ...`, `MakeError`, `FatalError`).

In fact, with these changes the conditional change of reject reason in `ValidationState::Error` is not needed, it is only called with a fresh Valid state, the `if` could be changed to an assert or removed. I haven't done so (just tried it).
